subject: Biotechnology
title: Prime Editing
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Prime Editing.

hook.text: Prime editing is the search-and-replace of genetics — it can make any small change without cutting both strands.

buildup.text: A modified Cas9 nicks one strand while a reverse transcriptase writes the new sequence directly into the DNA.

discovery.text: Prime editing can insert, delete, or swap any combination of bases — covering all 12 possible point mutations.

twist.text: Efficiency is still lower than standard CRISPR — making it work well in living organisms remains a challenge.

climax.text: Prime editing could theoretically correct 89% of known disease-causing mutations — the ultimate precision tool.

punchline.text: Search, find, rewrite — prime editing is gene editing's word processor.

quiz.question: What advantage does prime editing have over base editing?
options: It works faster and is more efficient in all cell types
It can make any small insertion, deletion, or substitution, not just single-base swaps
It does not require any guide RNA to find its target
